legal.headline: Bengaluru man moves Karnataka High Court to challenge seizure of his African grey parrot
legal.hook: Bengaluru man moves Karnataka High Court to challenge seizure of his African grey parrot
legal.summary: A resident of Bengaluru has filed a petition in the Karnataka High Court challenging the seizure of his African grey parrot, named 'Mithu', by the Forest Department. The petitioner, identified as Prashanth S, claims that the seizure was unlawful and that he has the necessary documentation to prove that the parrot was legally acquired. The Forest Department had taken the bird under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, asserting that African grey parrots are protected species and require permits for possession. Prashanth argues that the seizure violates his rights and has caused him emotional distress. The case is currently pending before the court, with Prashanth seeking the return of his pet and questioning the legality of the department's actions.
legal.contextNote: This case involves the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, specifically sections related to the possession and trade of protected species (Sections 9 and 51).
